How to Process an Access Request

Responsible Teams and Roles
IT Help Desk, System Owners, Compliance

Access Request Workflow Runbook

Purpose
This runbook standardizes the access request workflow for how internal system access requests are reviewed and fulfilled using least-privilege principles. It applies to new access, access changes, role transfers, and urgent temporary access.

When to Use
Use this runbook whenever an employee, manager, or system owner requests access to an internal application, mailbox, dashboard, shared drive, or administrative tool.

Responsible Roles
Primary owner: IT Help Desk or identity administrator.
Approvers: Manager, system owner, or data owner depending on resource sensitivity.
Supporting role: Compliance for sensitive-data or audit-impacting systems.

Procedure
Step 1: Confirm the requestor identity, target system, requested permission level, and stated business justification.
Step 2: Review the employee's current role and determine whether the requested access matches least-privilege expectations.
Step 3: Check whether an existing lower-privilege role or reporting view can satisfy the business need.
Step 4: Route the request to the correct approver based on the system's ownership and sensitivity.
Step 5: For urgent temporary access, record duration, reason, and expiration date before granting anything.
Step 6: Deny or hold the request if justification is incomplete, if approval is missing, or if the access exceeds role scope without exception approval.
Step 7: After approval, provision the access and verify that group membership, mailbox rights, or application permissions were applied correctly.
Step 8: Notify the requestor and manager of the outcome, including any restrictions or expiration date.
Step 9: Record the approval evidence, access granted, and date in the ticket or identity system.
Step 10: Schedule follow-up review for temporary or exceptional access so it does not remain open-ended.

Approval Requirements
Standard role-based access requires manager approval.
Sensitive systems containing PII, finance controls, or refund overrides require data-owner approval and may require Compliance review.
Privileged administrative access requires elevated approval and tighter logging.

Completion Criteria
The request is complete when access is provisioned or denied with evidence, stakeholders are informed, and review controls are documented.
